precepts.text: How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man. This was never heard of, women being over men. That is not the natural state, but you allow it. Cases come up where the brother does not know what is going on in his own house because his wife runs everything, and he is used to it.
precepts.point: Brothers, the same goes the other way: the moment you decide not to provide, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household. It is a domino effect. Some of you brothers did not want a wife; you wanted a mama.
precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

precepts.text: At the same time, saith the Lord, will I be the God of all the families of Israel. All the families in Genesis chapter 12 is all the families of Israel. This is why it's very important to go precept upon precept. There's no scripture that shows Christ came for all the families of the other nations.
precepts.point: Theology is a dangerous drug. These cemetery schools are dangerous for our community. White supremacy taught them the Bible; they get a certificate from going to school and learning their curriculum. We get a reward for doing God's law, statutes, and commandments: an everlasting reward with the father.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
The theology school men came preaching the promise of Genesis 12, that in Abraham all the families of the earth are blessed, as if it meant every nation. But “At the same time, saith the Lord, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.” All the families in Genesis chapter 12 are all the families of Israel.

That is why it is very important to go precept upon precept. There is no scripture that shows Christ came for all the families of the other nations. It is impossible.

Afterwards he was asked: name me one scripture where God named another nation by name that he is going to redeem or save in the last days. He said it ain't in there. So what are we talking about, then? God named Israel by name to be saved and redeemed, and no other nation in the New Testament.

So where are they getting it from? Theology is a dangerous drug. That is “another gospel, which ye have not accepted”, the gospel for all nations, and Paul says of those who receive it, “ye might well bear with him.”

precepts.text: Paul quotes this from Jeremiah. Christians avoid that, cuz when you ask them, so who's the new covenant for, it tells you crystal clear right there who it was for: the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not: meaning we went into slavery. When he says Israel right there, meaning all 12 tribes. I will put my laws into their mind: this is kingdom.
precepts.point: If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel. Nobody can measure heaven or search out all the places of the earth. So this is where Paul was getting it from.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Paul quotes this straight from Jeremiah: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. Christians avoid that, because when you ask them who the new covenant is for, it tells you crystal clear right there who it was for: the house of Israel and the house of Judah. He separates us like that because there was a split into two kingdoms, and when he says Israel right there, he means all 12 tribes.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt”. That was the old covenant, animal sacrifice. The 12 tribes are the bride and God is the husband. “because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord”: meaning we went into slavery.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. This is kingdom, the same promise Jeremiah gave. So this is the answer to replacement theology, the answer to supersessionism. The new covenant was never given to a church that took Israel's place; it was made with the same Israel that broke the first one.

And Jeremiah goes on to seal it: if the ordinances of the sun, the moon and the stars depart, then the seed of Israel ceases from being a nation. They have not departed, so the 12 tribes are still here to this day. Even in Paul's time the 12 tribes were there, yet Christians cannot point them out in the New Testament and say they are lost. It's all a lie. This is where Paul was getting it from.

precepts.text: Bring the books: the books meaning the books of Isaiah, the books of Jeremiah, the books of Micah. It's not talking about books about how to braid your hair. But especially the parchments: parchments are writing papers. So he would read the Old Testament books and base his epistles on those writings.
precepts.point: If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel. Nobody can measure heaven or search out all the places of the earth. So this is where Paul was getting it from.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Paul writes to Timothy: “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The books means the books of Isaiah, the books of Jeremiah, the books of Micah. It is not talking about books about how to braid your hair.

“but especially the parchments”: parchments are writing papers. Paul would read the Old Testament books and base his epistles on those writings. That is why Hebrews 8 carries the new covenant word for word out of Jeremiah 31: Paul was reading Jeremiah and writing from it.

So the New Testament does not replace the Old; it is built on it. When Jeremiah says the new covenant is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, and that the seed of Israel will not cease from being a nation while the sun, moon and stars stand, Paul was taking that from the prophets he carried with him. The church did not get a new covenant of its own; Paul was teaching Israel's covenant out of Israel's books.

precepts.text: Sing with gladness for Jacob and shout among the chief of the nations; O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel. I will bring them from the north country and gather them from the coasts of the earth, with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child; they shall come with weeping, and I will lead them by rivers of waters in a straight way, for I am a father to Israel and Ephraim is my firstborn.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.” Who is the lame? Jeremiah shows it: “For thus saith the Lord; Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” The Lord is not saving all Israelites; he is saving a remnant.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame”. The blind and the lame are Israel, with “the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.”

“They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.” Ephraim is the firstborn, meaning he was chosen over the northern kingdom.

So the lame that take the prey is Israel. When the tacklings of their ships are loosed and they cannot spread the sail, we are going to take the nations: we are going to prey on the nations.

precepts.text: The Most High giveth the sun for a light by day and the ordinances of the moon and stars for a light by night; if those ordinances depart from before him, then the seed of Israel shall cease from being a nation. They serve his children, not the reverse.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.
precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night”. The sun, moon and stars are ordinances: they keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept.

“If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” They serve his children, not the reverse. So why worship what the Most High created to serve you? Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept, not the sun, moon and stars.

That is the warning here: “lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them”. That is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt.

precepts.text: How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.
precepts.point: Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” At Ai, “all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand”. Women are casualties of war.

That stands as a warning for the sisters serving unrepented in the militaries of the nations, standing stiffly for the oppressor, a backsliding daughter compassing a man. When Christ comes back he is coming to kill, and a uniform and a weapon will not save; men and women will be dying alike, as they did at Ai. It is best in these last days for a woman to stand by and support her own man and her own nation, not another nation.

precepts.text: The Most High created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man; Vashti compassing the king is the very thing the wise men move to stop before it spreads.
precepts.point: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains, and the king was very wroth and his anger burned in him. She disrespected the king before everyone, and a judgment was now set to come.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” The Most High created a new thing in the earth: a woman shall compass a man.

That is Vashti. The king commanded his seven chamberlains “To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty”, and “the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by his chamberlains”. She disrespected the king before everyone, a woman compassing a man, and “therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.”

Vashti compassing the king is the very thing the wise men move to stop before it spreads, and a judgment was now set to come.

precepts.text: Israel will remain on this earth as long as the sun, moon, stars, and all the ordinances of heaven are still in place.
precepts.point: He shall have dominion from sea to sea and from the river unto the ends of the earth, meaning he will rule the entire planet.

note.label: Psalm 72: All Nations Shall Serve Him

precepts.why:
“They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.” The poor of his people will fear the Most High and keep his commandments throughout all generations, as long as the sun and moon endure. Jeremiah shows why the sun and moon are the measure: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

Israel will remain on this earth as long as the sun, moon, stars and all the ordinances of heaven are still in place. Only if those ordinances depart would the seed of Israel cease from being a nation, and they have not departed.

So the people who fear him as long as the sun and moon endure are Israel, and the king's son who “shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth” will rule the entire planet over them, with “abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.”

precepts.text: Just like the sun, moon, and sky are a witness, the Lord has not forsaken His chosen people.
precepts.point: This is the visiting of iniquity in the regeneration; after death comes the judgment, when you reform your mind and subdue your own understanding, and you will be kept alive and obtain mercy.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
The throne of David is “established for ever as the moon, and as a faithful witness in heaven.” Jeremiah shows why the heavens are the witness: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

Just like the sun, moon and sky are a witness, the Lord has not forsaken his chosen people. Look up: the sun still gives light by day and the moon and stars by night. As long as those ordinances stand, the seed of Israel has not ceased from being a nation before him.

That is the covenant he will not break nor alter. Even when his children are visited with the rod and stripes, the faithful witness in heaven is still shining, and so David's seed and Israel endure.

precepts.text: The decree that shall not pass: as long as the sun, moon, and stars keep their ordinances, the seed of Israel shall not cease from being a nation before Him forever.
precepts.point: Let them praise the name of the Most High, for He commanded and they were created. All these things He created obey Him. He hath also stablished them forever and ever; He hath made a decree which shall not pass.

note.label: Psalm 148: He Exalteth the Horn of His People

precepts.why:
“He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.” Here is that decree: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

As long as the nation of Israel is on this earth, these ordinances will stay and do the jobs they were given, serving for a light by night and by day. Even the heavens, the sun, the moon, and the stars are not here for decoration; they are here for a purpose, used for signs and for seasons. All these things he created obey him.

precepts.text: The Most High likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman, and that comely delicate woman is Israel.
precepts.point: He appeared of old saying He loved them with an everlasting love and with lovingkindness drew them; again He will build the virgin of Israel, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances, planting vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.
precepts.why:
The Lord says “Again I will build thee, and thou shalt be built, O virgin of Israel”, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances of them that make merry. Earlier in Jeremiah he tells who that virgin is: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

That comely and delicate woman is Israel. The daughter of Zion, the virgin of Israel, is the people he loved with an everlasting love and drew with lovingkindness, the same people left of the sword that found grace in the wilderness. He will build her again, and she will plant vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.

precepts.text: Stand in the ways and ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk therein to find rest for your souls, though they said we will not; the old paths are keeping God's laws.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.
precepts.why:
The Lord will lead the gathered remnant “in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble”. That straight way is keeping God's laws. He had told our fathers where to find it: “Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.”

The old paths are keeping God's laws; that is the good way and the rest for our souls. “But they said, We will not walk therein.” Our fathers refused the old paths, and that is why Israel had to be brought back from the north country with weeping and supplications. When he gathers them he leads them in that same straight way himself.

precepts.text: The entrance is narrow, set in a dangerous place with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left, one only path between them for one man to walk.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.
precepts.why:
The straight way the Lord leads Israel in is not a wide one. Ezra describes it: “The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”.

“And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.” Fire on the right hand, deep water on the left, and one only path between them for one man to walk. That is the straight way of Jeremiah 31:9, keeping God's laws, wherein they shall not stumble because he leads them by the rivers of waters.

precepts.text: Wide is the gate and broad the way that leadeth to destruction which many find, but strait is the gate and narrow the way which leadeth unto life, and few find it.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.
precepts.why:
Christ says the same thing about the way: “Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat”.

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.” Wide is the gate and broad the way to destruction, and many find it; the narrow way to life, few find. It is the one only path between the fire and the water in 2 Esdras 7, and the straight way of Jeremiah 31:9. Keeping God's laws is the narrow way, and that is the way he causes the remnant of Israel to walk in.

precepts.text: Also He will make him His firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth, that is, higher than the other nations.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.
precepts.why:
“For I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.” Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High. The psalm tells what the firstborn is set over: “Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.”

Higher than the kings of the earth means higher than the other nations. So all of Israel shall be over all the nations. Ephraim was singled out because the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel: the whole remnant the Lord gathers from the coasts of the earth is his firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.

precepts.text: The ox knoweth his owner and the ass his master's crib, but Israel does not know; most of our people do not consider that they are Israel.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.
precepts.why:
The Lord is a father to Israel and Ephraim is his firstborn, yet most of our people do not know it. Isaiah says it plainly: “The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.”

An ox knows who owns him and an ass knows where his master feeds him, but Israel does not know. Most of our people do not consider that they are Israel, the remnant the Lord is gathering from the north country and the coasts of the earth. That is why the call goes out to publish and praise and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.

precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord that created thee O Jacob and formed thee O Israel, fear not, for I have redeemed thee and called thee by thy name, thou art mine.
precepts.point: Both young men and old shall rejoice in the dance, for He will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and satiate the soul of the priest with fatness, and His people shall be satisfied with His goodness.
precepts.why:
“For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.” Isaiah says who did the redeeming and who was redeemed: “But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.”

He that created Jacob and formed Israel is the one that redeemed him. He called Israel by name, and Israel is his. So the nations are to hear and declare it in the isles afar off: he that scattered Israel will gather him and keep him as a shepherd does his flock, and they shall come and sing in the height of Zion and sorrow no more, because they belong to him.

precepts.text: Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they were not.
precepts.point: The mourning in Ramah was written of beforehand by Jeremiah.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
Matthew says the mourning in Rama was “that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet”, and here is where Jeremiah spoke it: “A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not.”

The weeping and great mourning for the children was written of beforehand. Rachel refusing to be comforted, because her children were not, is the very thing Matthew records being fulfilled. The prophet saw it long before it came to pass, and it fell out word for word.

precepts.text: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah.
precepts.point: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
Christ took the cup after supper and said, “This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.” Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

Jeremiah: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah”. The new covenant, the new testament in his blood, was promised to the house of Israel and the house of Judah. That is who Christ sat down with at that passover, the twelve apostles, and that is who the blood was shed for.

precepts.text: The Most High will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and Judah.
precepts.point: Christ did only what the Most High intended, to make His soul an offering for sin. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary and that obedience and mercy were desired above it.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah”. The new covenant was promised in the old testament, to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

So when the sacrifice and offerings were set aside, Christ was not changing the customs Moses delivered, as the false witnesses said. He was doing what the Most High had already said he would do; it is written throughout the old testament.

precepts.text: The covenant with the house of Israel: he writes the law in their hearts, forgives their iniquity, and remembers their sin no more.
precepts.point: Remission of sins, the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Remission of sins is the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, and it is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. “But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.”

“For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.” The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more. That is the remission of sins Peter preached in Cornelius' house.
